description.blurb: With a shape resembling a chicken leg, the nucleus of comet 19P/Borrelly is approximately 5 miles (8 kilometers) long. Deep Space 1 encountered comet Borrelly on Sept. 22, 2001.
description.more:
In a risky flyby, NASA's Deep Space 1 spacecraft successfully navigated past comet Borrelly, giving researchers the best look ever inside the glowing core of icy dust and gas.

The space probe's close encounter with comet Borrelly provided the best-resolution pictures of any comet to date. The already-successful Deep Space 1, without protection from the little-known comet environment, whizzes by just 2,200 kilometers from the rocky, icy nucleus of the 10-kilometer-long comet.
